measuredIn: a full clone of the second independent golden-image build
method: Each provider's credential files were copied from the standing switchyard-agent vault into /Users/switchyard, then that provider's own auth check was run inside the guest through launchctl asuser <uid> sudo -iu switchyard. Attribution is per file: each file was moved aside and the check re-run, so every tarProvisionable:true below names the file that actually decides the verdict. Exit status is not the classifier -- cursor-agent and opencode both exit 0 while logged out.

claude.evidence: Both files are required. With either one alone the check reports "loggedIn": false, "authMethod": "none"; with both it reports "loggedIn": true, "authMethod": "claude.ai".

codex.evidence: Without the file the check reports Not logged in.

agy.evidence: File-backed despite appearances: agy writes a gemini login-Keychain entry after authenticating (absent at baseline, present after), yet still fails with 'Please sign in to view available models' when only the token file is removed. Keychain presence is not evidence of Keychain backing.

copilot.evidence: This falsified the standing prediction. copilot login --help advertises the system credential store, which on macOS is the login Keychain, and copilot was called the most likely Keychain-backed no. It is file-backed: removing the file yields 'Error: No authentication information found.' and a copied file authenticates.

opencode.evidence: Without the file the check reports 0 credentials, at exit status 0.

cursor-agent.evidence: The PM3-5 case this column exists to catch: file-backed in shape, machine-bound in behavior. With .config/cursor/auth.json, .cursor/cli-config.json, and .cursor/agent-cli-state.json all provisioned, the check still reports Not logged in, and no cursor-related service appeared in the login Keychain.
